PROBLEM: Client and server may speak different protocol eras; naive version pinning breaks interop while naive fallback masks genuine incompatibility.
MECHANISM: mode=auto probes server/discover at the newest modern version. Anything that is not positive evidence of a modern peer falls back to the legacy initialize handshake (denylist, not allowlist). -32022 carrying a disjoint modern-only supported list raises. Transport and network errors propagate as-is and are never treated as era verdicts. Source: src/mcp/client/_probe.py (module docstring and negotiate_auto).
INVARIANT: Genuine incompatibility always surfaces as an explicit error; ambiguous failures always fall back, never produce era verdicts.
FAILURE_MODEL: A probe that times out client-side but succeeds on a slow-starting server can lock the connection modern before the pipelined initialize arrives; handled by one corrective re-probe at a mutual version instead of failing the connect.
SECURITY_MODEL: Downgrade is bounded: fallback goes only to the legacy handshake, never below it; disjoint-modern peers raise instead of silently downgrading.
SCALING_MODEL: One extra round trip per connection; a prior DiscoverResult can be reused via prior_discover.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has no tool protocol at all (proven gap: zero tool-call records repo-wide). If CRX ever speaks MCP as an adapter, this is the version-drift pattern for the TOOL RESOLUTION link.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool references would gain a protocol-era dimension; resolution negotiates era before first call rather than assuming it.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: era table plus probe-then-handshake in the (future) CRX MCP client.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Prevents silent version-skew breakage when CRX adopts external tool servers; converts drift into typed errors.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Point an SDK v2 client at a server advertising only a disjoint modern version and assert MCPError -32022. Point it at a dead port and assert a transport error, not an era verdict.

PROBLEM: Servers self-describe tool safety (read-only, destructive, idempotent); clients must not treat self-attestation as trust.
MECHANISM: ToolAnnotations{title, readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint} is carried on Tool. The spec text in source states all properties are hints, not guaranteed faithful, and clients should never make tool-use decisions based on ToolAnnotations received from untrusted servers. Source: src/mcp-types/mcp_types/_v2026_07_28/__init__.py:1076.
INVARIANT: Annotations inform UX and heuristics; they never grant authority.
FAILURE_MODEL: A malicious server sets readOnlyHint=true on a destructive tool; any client that auto-approves on hints is fully compromised.
SECURITY_MODEL: Self-attested metadata is untrusted input, in the same threat class as tool descriptions (prompt-injection/poisoning surface).
SCALING_MODEL: Zero marginal cost; piggybacked on tools/list.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ToolAuthority/ToolGateway exist with zero callers. When built, tool metadata must be evidence-graded (CONFIRMED vs self-attested), never trusted at face value, per the standing stack-claim grading rule.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool registry gains an annotation-trust field: SELF_ATTESTED vs VERIFIED; only VERIFIED may influence authorization-adjacent heuristics.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a trust-grade field plus a lint rule forbidding hint-based auto-approval.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Prevents a whole class of confused-deputy auto-approval bugs before CRX writes its first tool-authorization line.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Serve a tool with readOnlyHint=true that deletes a file; assert the reference client still requires explicit authorization.

PROBLEM: Bearer tokens need validation, expiry enforcement, audience binding, and scope checks at the transport edge.
MECHANISM: BearerAuthMiddleware validates via a TokenVerifier, rejects tokens past expires_at, rejects tokens whose resource does not URL-match resource_server_url (audience binding via _issued_for_this_resource), and redacts tokens in logs. RequireAuthMiddleware enforces per-route required_scopes: 401 invalid_token / 403 insufficient_scope with WWW-Authenticate. Source: src/mcp/server/auth/middleware/bearer_auth.py.
INVARIANT: No token, an expired token, or a wrong-resource token ever reaches a handler; scope failures are 403, never ambiguous.
FAILURE_MODEL: TokenVerifier is a protocol and audience/issuer enforcement is explicitly up to the verifier; the bundled ProviderTokenVerifier only loads the token from the provider, so default deployments do not cryptographically verify audience unless the operator implements it.
SECURITY_MODEL: Audience binding blocks token replay across resource servers; log redaction blocks credential leakage through diagnostics.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-request async verification; cacheable inside the verifier implementation.
CRX_ANALOG: AUTHORIZATION link. CRX has no credential validation on tool calls; this is the concrete shape: authenticate at the edge, authorize per scope, fail closed, redact in logs.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool invocations gain a credential-validation step ahead of ToolAuthority; token material never appears in canonical events or logs.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: verifier implementation plus middleware placement; the fail-open default verifier must be replaced, not inherited.
EXPECTED_VALUE: A reviewed, concrete OAuth edge pattern instead of a hand-rolled one.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Present an expired token and assert rejection; present a token with a mismatched resource and assert rejection plus a warning log with the token redacted.

PROBLEM: Abandoned tool calls (caller timeout, task cancellation) keep consuming server resources while nobody wants the result.
MECHANISM: RequestOptions.cancel_on_abandon (default True): when the caller abandons a request through timeout or cancellation, the client sends notifications/cancelled; initialize is excluded because the protocol forbids cancelling it. Source: src/mcp/shared/dispatcher.py:95-100.
INVARIANT: Every abandonment is signaled unless the protocol forbids it.
FAILURE_MODEL: The notification is best-effort and may be lost on a dead transport; the server may still complete the work. Cancellation is advisory, not a kill.
SECURITY_MODEL: Bounds resource exhaustion from abandoned long-running calls; no authentication implications.
SCALING_MODEL: O(1) per request.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link. CRX WorkerRuntime results reify as canonical events, but the proven gap is that NOT STARTED/STARTED/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/TIMED_OUT/CANCELLED/UNKNOWN are indistinguishable. CANCELLED must become a first-class terminal state with a causation link to the abandoning event.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool-call lifecycle gains explicit CANCELLED; abandonment emits a canonical event rather than vanishing.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a terminal state plus a cancellation signal on the worker boundary.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Typed cancellation semantics for the missing CRX tool-call lifecycle; no more silent abandonment.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Start a long tool call, cancel the caller scope, and assert notifications/cancelled is emitted on the wire.

PROBLEM: SSE streams break on server disappearance or network blips; naive clients lose in-flight progress and duplicate side effects on retry.
MECHANISM: The StreamableHTTP client tracks the SSE retry field; on stream break it waits (server-provided interval or 1000 ms default) and reconnects with Last-Event-ID for resume. MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS=2, then the error surfaces to the caller. Source: src/mcp/client/streamable_http.py:59-60,222-264,459-575.
INVARIANT: Resume is event-ID based, never blind replay; attempts are strictly bounded.
FAILURE_MODEL: After 2 attempts the error surfaces; there is no server-side dedup, so non-idempotent tools may double-execute if the server processed the original request.
SECURITY_MODEL: Reconnect reuses the original auth context; no credential re-prompt, no privilege change across resume.
SCALING_MODEL: Bounded: at most 2 retries with ~1s delays per break.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link, server-disappearance handling. CRX subagents are disposable with automatic result delivery; MCP tool calls need the same bounded-resume discipline.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX transport layer gains resume tokens; tool calls must be marked idempotent or non-retryable (paired with idempotentHint, M02).
INTEGRATION_COST: M: resume-token plumbing plus idempotency marking on tool defs.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Prevents retry storms and duplicate side effects when tool servers disappear mid-call.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Kill the SSE stream mid tool-call; assert exactly one reconnect carrying Last-Event-ID and at most 2 attempts total.

PROBLEM: Tool calls can hang forever; hung calls pin workers and mask server death.
MECHANISM: Layered, explicit bounds: client read_timeout_seconds per tools/call round, init_timeout for the handshake, disconnect_timeout; server session_idle_timeout (DEFAULT_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT) and request_read_timeout_seconds. 0 disables a bound explicitly, never accidentally. Source: src/mcp/client/client.py:755, src/mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:730, src/mcp/server/session.py:97-114.
INVARIANT: Every wait has a bound; disabling a bound is always an explicit opt-out.
FAILURE_MODEL: No server-side bound on tool handler execution time was found in SDK v2; timeouts cover reads and idleness, not execution. A hung handler holds the session.
SECURITY_MODEL: Timeouts bound slow-server resource exhaustion (slowloris class) on both sides.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-request timers; negligible overhead.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link. CRX needs TIMED_OUT as a terminal state distinct from FAILED, with the budget recorded on the call.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool-call records gain timeout budget fields; expiry emits a canonical TIMED_OUT event with causation.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: budget fields plus timer enforcement on the worker boundary.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Basic liveness hygiene CRX currently lacks for tools; converts hangs into typed events.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Call a tool that sleeps longer than read_timeout_seconds; assert TimeoutError and a notifications/cancelled emission.

PROBLEM: A tool call may need human input mid-execution (approval, missing parameter); naive designs block forever or lose resumability across restarts.
MECHANISM: The server returns InputRequiredResult; the client dispatches embedded input requests to sampling/elicitation/roots callbacks and retries the call automatically up to input_required_max_rounds. request_state can be persisted across process restarts, subject to server TTL, request binding, and key lifetime. Elicitation outcomes are typed: accept, decline, cancel, URL mode. Source: src/mcp/client/client.py:751-796, src/mcp/server/elicitation.py.
INVARIANT: Input rounds are strictly bounded; restart-resume is explicit and server-consented, never assumed.
FAILURE_MODEL: A server on the default process-local key rejects resumed state after a restart; resume is best-effort and the caller must handle re-elicitation.
SECURITY_MODEL: Elicitation is the human-in-the-loop authorization hook: a server can request confirmation before a destructive step without the client pre-authorizing the whole call.
SCALING_MODEL: Bounded rounds; state persisted only when the host opts in.
CRX_ANALOG: AUTHORIZATION link. CRX autonomous missions need a typed waiting-on-human state with resume tokens; this is the pattern.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool-call lifecycle gains SUSPENDED_AWAITING_INPUT with a resumable, TTL-bound token.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: suspension state, resume tokens, and a bounded retry loop in the mission runtime.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Human-gated destructive tools without breaking autonomy for safe ones; restarts do not lose the thread.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Have a server request input twice then succeed; assert the client retries exactly twice and returns the result. Exceed max rounds and assert InputRequiredRoundsExceededError.

PROBLEM: Hosts need extra result shapes on tools/call without forking the protocol or colliding with future spec vocabulary.
MECHANISM: ResultClaim{result_type, model, resolve, method, protocol_versions}: host-registered claims attach extra result shapes to tools/call. Construction-time guards: claims only on allowlisted methods, models must subclass mcp_types.Result but not core result types, wire aliases may not collide with core fields, protocol_versions must be modern. Source: src/mcp/client/extension.py.
INVARIANT: Extensions can never shadow or break core protocol vocabulary; version-gated claims never activate on legacy wires.
FAILURE_MODEL: A misconfigured claim raises at construction (fail fast), never at call time.
SECURITY_MODEL: Claims are host-registered; a malicious server cannot inject a claim, it can only send resultTypes the host already handles.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-client construction cost; zero per-call cost when inactive.
CRX_ANALOG: RECEIPT link. CRX reifies worker results as canonical events; claims are the discipline for typed receipt enrichment without forking the event schema.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: None required now; adopt the guard pattern (no shadowing, version-gated) when CRX adds receipt subtypes.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: construction-time validation rules for receipt extensions.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Safe extension discipline: richer receipts without protocol-fork risk.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Register a claim whose model aliases a core result field; assert ValueError at construction.

PROBLEM: Cached tool catalogs go stale when servers add or remove tools; stale catalogs cause misrouted calls.
MECHANISM: The server sends notifications/tools/list_changed; the client invalidates cached listings (the response cache re-absorbs served listings idempotently). Source: src/mcp/server/session.py:461, src/mcp/server/connection.py:441, src/mcp/client/session.py:1294.
INVARIANT: Discovery is never trusted past an invalidation signal.
FAILURE_MODEL: A lost notification on a broken transport leaves a staleness window until reconnect; the SDK has no poll fallback.
SECURITY_MODEL: A compromised server can spam list_changed to thrash client caches (minor DoS); notifications carry no auth beyond the transport.
SCALING_MODEL: O(1) signal; re-list cost only on invalidation.
CRX_ANALOG: TOOL RESOLUTION link: tool health. A CRX ToolGateway should treat listings as leases, not facts.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool catalog entries gain freshness and lease semantics; invalidation is an event, not a silent refresh.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: invalidation signal handling plus lease timestamps on catalog entries.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Prevents stale-tool misrouting, the quietest failure in multi-server setups.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Have a server add a tool and notify; assert the client re-lists before its next call.

PROBLEM: Bidirectional progress doubles protocol surface and creates backpressure ambiguity about who reports to whom.
MECHANISM: Since protocol version 2026-07-28, progress is server-to-client only; client-to-server progress is deprecated. Source: src/mcp/client/client.py:530 and surrounding deprecation note.
INVARIANT: Progress flows one way: executor to requester.
FAILURE_MODEL: Old clients sending client progress hit the deprecation path, not hard errors (lenient migration).
SECURITY_MODEL: Removes a channel a client could use to steer server execution via progress payloads.
SCALING_MODEL: Halves the notification surface.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link: progress reporting from CRX workers to the mission should follow the same direction.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX worker progress events flow worker-to-mission only; mission-to-worker progress is not a concept.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a direction rule in the progress event schema.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Simpler, safer progress semantics; one fewer confused-deputy channel.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Negotiate 2026-07-28 and send client-to-server progress; assert the deprecation path is taken.

PROBLEM: Mutable (name, version) pairs let a published tool change behavior under a pinned reference: rug-pull at the registry layer.
MECHANISM: Publish rejects duplicate (name, version) with invalid version: cannot publish duplicate version: {name}@{version} already exists (ErrInvalidVersion). Behavior changes require minting a new version. Source: internal/service/registry_service.go:193; migration 009 notes immutable server.json.
INVARIANT: A resolved (name, version) always denotes the same metadata.
FAILURE_MODEL: None for readers; publishers must practice semver discipline, which the registry does not enforce beyond uniqueness.
SECURITY_MODEL: Removes registry-layer rug-pull; shifts trust to the version-minting identity, which is covered by namespace auth (M13).
SCALING_MODEL: Database uniqueness constraint; O(1) check.
CRX_ANALOG: TOOL RESOLUTION. CRX tool references should be content-pinned (name, version) immutable pairs.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX ToolGateway resolution becomes immutable: re-resolving a pinned ref is a cache hit, never a re-fetch.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a uniqueness constraint on (tool_name, tool_version) at registration.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Eliminates an entire drift class at the resolution layer for near-zero cost.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Publish example/test-server@1.0.0 twice; assert the second publish fails with the duplicate-version error.

PROBLEM: Version ranges (^1.2.3, latest) make installs non-reproducible and widen the supply-chain attack surface.
MECHANISM: The server.json schema rejects version ranges and the literal latest for package versions; server versions SHOULD follow semver. Source: docs/reference/server-json/draft/server.schema.json:284-290, 479-482.
INVARIANT: Every install resolves to an exact, auditable version.
FAILURE_MODEL: Publishers who want to move fast must mint versions explicitly; there is no floating.
SECURITY_MODEL: Narrows supply-chain substitution attacks to the exact pinned artifact.
SCALING_MODEL: Schema validation at publish time; zero runtime cost.
CRX_ANALOG: TOOL RESOLUTION. CRX mission tool dependencies should pin exact versions.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool manifests reject ranges at canonicalization time (fail-closed ingress, matching CRX's existing ingress doctrine).
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a schema rule in the tool manifest validator.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Reproducible tool environments; no floating dependencies in autonomous missions.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Submit a server.json with package version ^1.2.3; assert schema validation rejects it.

PROBLEM: Without namespace ownership proof, anyone can publish under any server name: impersonation and name-squatting poison discovery.
MECHANISM: Publishers prove namespace control through one of: DNS TXT with ed25519 challenge signing (v=MCPv1), GitHub OIDC, GitHub device flow, or Azure KeyVault / Google KMS key custody. No publish without proof. Source: cmd/publisher/auth/ (dns.go, github-oidc.go, github-at.go, azurekeyvault/, googlekms/).
INVARIANT: No publish without proof of namespace control.
FAILURE_MODEL: DNS propagation delays block publishing; key loss means namespace loss (no recovery path found in the inspected code).
SECURITY_MODEL: Binds a registry name to a proven identity; package ownership verification (M14) additionally binds the artifacts.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-publish challenge; keys cached client-side.
CRX_ANALOG: TOOL RESOLUTION identity. A CRX tool registry needs publisher identity binding before tools enter the catalog.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool registration requires namespace proof; anonymous tools are quarantined, never catalogued.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: challenge-response flow plus key custody for CRX-published tools.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Impersonation-resistant tool discovery; the registry cannot be name-squatted.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Attempt to publish com.example/server without the DNS TXT proof; assert rejection.

PROBLEM: A registry entry can point at an artifact the publisher does not control: impersonation via metadata.
MECHANISM: The official registry requires proof of package ownership per registry type (e.g., an mcp-name tag in the PyPI README) and accepts only allowlisted public base URLs: registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, api.nuget.org, crates.io, docker.io, ghcr.io, quay.io, *.pkg.dev, *.azurecr.io, mcr.microsoft.com, and github/gitlab releases for MCPB. Source: docs/reference/server-json/official-registry-requirements.md.
INVARIANT: Registry metadata always resolves to publisher-controlled artifacts on allowlisted registries.
FAILURE_MODEL: Private registries are unsupported; air-gapped enterprises need sub-registries, which the spec explicitly supports.
SECURITY_MODEL: Closes metadata-to-artifact substitution; the allowlist shrinks mirror-confusion attacks.
SCALING_MODEL: Publish-time verification; zero runtime cost.
CRX_ANALOG: TOOL RESOLUTION supply chain for CRX tool artifacts.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool artifacts resolve only from allowlisted sources and only with ownership proof recorded.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: ownership-verification checks per artifact source plus an allowlist.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Supply-chain integrity for tool binaries: what the catalog names is what the publisher controls.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Publish an entry pointing at an unverified PyPI package; assert rejection.

PROBLEM: Server configs need secrets at install time without baking them into published metadata.
MECHANISM: server.json inputs carry isSecret (advisory: clients should handle the value securely) and {variable} substitution in values, resolved client-side at install. Source: docs/reference/server-json/draft/server.schema.json:104-106 and the InputWithVariables definition.
INVARIANT: Secrets are declared, never embedded; substitution happens client-side at install time.
FAILURE_MODEL: Advisory only: a careless client can log the value and the registry will not stop it. The registry enforces declaration, not handling.
SECURITY_MODEL: Weak on its own; real protection comes from client secret stores (see M22).
SCALING_MODEL: Zero runtime cost.
CRX_ANALOG: Credential handling for CRX tool configs. CRX must do better than advisory: enforcement, not hints.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool config schema gains secret-typed fields with enforced redaction at every display and log boundary.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: the declaration pattern; enforcement is additional work.
EXPECTED_VALUE: A clean declaration pattern for install-time secrets; the gap it leaves is documented, not inherited blindly.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Publish a server.json with a literal token in env instead of a variable; assert it is accepted, documenting that the flag is advisory.

PROBLEM: Merging tool sets from N servers causes name collisions; last-writer-wins silently misroutes calls.
MECHANISM: The gateway prefixes every tool with its server: prefix + __ + toolName, where the prefix comes from server config or the server name when the tool-name-prefix feature is enabled. Source: pkg/gateway/capabilitites.go:77-100,164-177.
INVARIANT: Tool identity is (server, name); collisions are impossible by construction.
FAILURE_MODEL: Renames break clients that hardcoded unprefixed names; migration is explicit.
SECURITY_MODEL: Prevents cross-server tool shadowing, where one server hijacks another server's trusted tool name.
SCALING_MODEL: O(N) rename at discovery.
CRX_ANALOG: TOOL RESOLUTION. A CRX ToolGateway merging multiple servers needs namespaced tool identities.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool IDs become (namespace, name) pairs; unqualified names are resolved, never assumed.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a namespacing rule in the merge step.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Eliminates tool shadowing by construction; the cheapest high-value mechanism in the gateway.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Enable two servers that both expose search; assert the merged catalog exposes two distinct prefixed tools and that calls route to the correct server.

PROBLEM: Cross-cutting concerns (telemetry, secret blocking, logging, custom policy) need ordered, auditable composition around tool calls.
MECHANISM: Callbacks(logCalls, blockSecrets, oauthInterceptorEnabled, interceptors) builds an ordered middleware chain: telemetry always-on, then OAuth interceptors, then custom before/after/around interceptors (exec, docker image, or HTTP specs), then BlockSecrets placed before logging so diagnostics never observe secrets, then LogCalls. Source: pkg/interceptors/interceptors.go.
INVARIANT: Telemetry cannot be disabled; secret scanning always precedes diagnostic logging by construction.
FAILURE_MODEL: A misordered custom interceptor could log before secret blocking; the fixed ordering of built-ins bounds this risk.
SECURITY_MODEL: Defense in depth by construction; custom interceptors are explicit CLI specs, hence auditable.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-call middleware stack; linear in chain length.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link. CRX WorkerRuntime needs an ordered interceptor chain around tool execution with mandatory positions.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool execution gains a middleware pipeline where audit and secret-scan positions are mandatory and ordered.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: a middleware-chain abstraction on the CRX worker boundary.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Auditable, ordered cross-cutting enforcement instead of ad-hoc wrappers.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Enable blockSecrets and logCalls, pass a secret in arguments, and assert the call is blocked and the secret never appears in logs.

PROBLEM: Agents paste secrets into tool arguments and servers echo secrets in results; both leak into logs and model context.
MECHANISM: BlockSecretsMiddleware scans tools/call arguments and responses with secretsscan rules and blocks the call (a secret is being passed to tool %s) when arguments contain secrets; responses are scanned post-call. Source: pkg/interceptors/block_secrets.go; pkg/secretsscan.
INVARIANT: A detected secret never traverses the tool boundary in either direction.
FAILURE_MODEL: Pattern-based detection has false negatives on novel formats and false positives that block legitimate calls; it fails closed, erring toward blocking.
SECURITY_MODEL: Blocks credential exfiltration via tool calls and via tool results into model context.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-call string scan; linear in payload size.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION and RECEIPT links. CRX canonicalization at ingress is already fail-closed; tool I/O needs the same treatment.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool-call ingress and egress gain secret scanning as a canonicalization step; detections become typed events.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a secret-scan rule set plus a block-before-execute hook.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Concrete, tested secret-boundary enforcement in both directions.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Call a tool with an AWS-style key in arguments; assert the call is blocked with the named error and no secret material reaches logs.

PROBLEM: Diagnostic logs of tool calls must not become a covert credential store.
MECHANISM: LogCallsMiddleware logs tool name, arguments, response, and duration only when --log-calls is enabled, and it runs after BlockSecrets by fixed chain order so diagnostics never observe secrets. Source: pkg/interceptors/interceptors.go (chain order), pkg/interceptors/log_calls.go.
INVARIANT: No enabled diagnostic ever sees a secret; logging is off by default.
FAILURE_MODEL: Custom interceptors can be ordered by the operator before BlockSecrets, recreating the leak; the built-in order protects only the defaults.
SECURITY_MODEL: Ordered defense: secret-scan is a mandatory predecessor of diagnostic logging.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-call log volume only when enabled.
CRX_ANALOG: RECEIPT link. CRX structured request logging (M31) must keep the same order: redact before record.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: None new; this is the ordering constraint that M18 and M31 depend on.

EXPECTED_VALUE: A documented anti-leak ordering rule; cheap to adopt, expensive to rediscover.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Enable logCalls without blockSecrets, call a tool with a secret in arguments, and assert the secret is logged: this documents why the two must be co-enabled in the correct order.

PROBLEM: The tool layer needs policy decisions (allow/deny) without becoming the policy author.
MECHANISM: The gateway queries an external PolicyClient for allow/deny; decisions are made outside the adapter. The bundled NoopClient is fail-open and always allows, which is explicitly the operator's responsibility to replace. Source: pkg/policy/policy.go.
INVARIANT: Authorization lives outside the tool layer; the gateway only enforces the answer.
FAILURE_MODEL: Operators who leave NoopClient in place run fail-open; a policy-service outage must be handled by the operator's client, and fail-closed should be the default.
SECURITY_MODEL: This is the canonical anti-pattern boundary: the adapter enforces, it never decides. Any design letting the tool layer decide authorization is REJECT by the harvest rule.
SCALING_MODEL: One policy round trip per call; cacheable.
CRX_ANALOG: AUTHORIZATION link. CRX ToolAuthority must be an external decider to the tool gateway, never the gateway deciding for itself.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool calls carry an authorization receipt: policy source, decision, and timestamp, separate from execution.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: a policy-client interface plus an authorization-receipt record on every call.
EXPECTED_VALUE: The correct separation of powers: adapter enforces, authority decides; with an explicit fail-open trap documented.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Run the gateway with the default NoopClient and a destructive tool; assert it is allowed, documenting that the default is fail-open and must be replaced.

PROBLEM: Tool servers distributed as container images can be tampered with between publish and execution.
MECHANISM: The gateway verifies container image signatures via Sigstore before the tool server runs. Source: pkg/signatures/signatures.go.
INVARIANT: An unsigned or bad-signature image never executes.
FAILURE_MODEL: Key compromise upstream breaks the chain; verification adds pull latency.
SECURITY_MODEL: Supply-chain integrity at the execution boundary: the artifact that runs is the artifact that was signed.
SCALING_MODEL: Verification per image pull; cacheable.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link: artifact verification before CRX workers execute third-party tool code.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool server manifests gain signature fields; verification precedes first execution.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: Sigstore verification integrated into the tool-server launch path.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Concrete supply-chain verification at the exact point where untrusted code becomes trusted execution.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Present an image with a bad signature; assert the gateway refuses to launch it.

PROBLEM: OAuth tokens for tool servers must live somewhere that is not a plaintext config file or a log line.
MECHANISM: OAuth tokens are stored in the OS keychain via the OAuth interceptor flow, so tokens are not persisted in config or logs. Source: pkg/oauth/ (token store handling observed during inspection).
INVARIANT: Token material never touches files or logs the gateway owns.
FAILURE_MODEL: Keychain unavailable (headless environments) breaks the OAuth flow; a fallback would recreate the storage problem.
SECURITY_MODEL: Delegates secret custody to the OS trust boundary instead of the application.
SCALING_MODEL: OS-keychain lookup per session; negligible.
CRX_ANALOG: Credential custody for CRX tool-server OAuth. Tokens belong in the Secure Vault / OS keychain, never in mission configs.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool configs reference credential slots, never credential values.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: keychain integration; CRX already has a Secure Vault doctrine to align with.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Platform-backed token custody; watch rather than adopt until the keychain-dependency failure mode is resolved for headless runtimes.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Run the OAuth flow on a machine with a locked keychain; assert the flow fails closed rather than writing tokens to disk.

PROBLEM: A compromised or over-broad server exposes tools the agent should never see; discovery-time filtering must reduce the attack surface before authorization.
MECHANISM: The gateway's startup allowlist (docker-mcp gateway run with tool restrictions) filters the tool catalog at discovery: unlisted tools are never merged and never callable. Source: cmd/docker-mcp/commands/gateway.go (allowlist/denylist flag handling observed during inspection).
INVARIANT: What is not listed at startup does not exist at runtime.
FAILURE_MODEL: Over-restrictive lists break legitimate workflows; under-restrictive lists recreate the exposure problem. Lists are static per run.
SECURITY_MODEL: Discovery-time least privilege: authorization (M26) is the second gate, but the catalog itself is already minimal.
SCALING_MODEL: O(N) filter at startup; zero per-call cost.
CRX_ANALOG: AUTHORIZATION link, first gate. A CRX ToolGateway should apply a mission-scoped tool allowlist before any tool is resolvable.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX mission manifests declare tool allowlists; the gateway merges only listed tools.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: an allowlist field plus a merge-time filter.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Defense in depth at discovery: even a confused-deputy authorization bug can only reach listed tools.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Start the gateway with an allowlist omitting a server tool; assert the tool is absent from the merged catalog and uncallable.

PROBLEM: Tool servers are untrusted code; a compromised server can pivot into the network or exfiltrate data.
MECHANISM: Per-server network isolation: disableNetwork blocks all egress for the tool server; allowHosts restricts to a named allowlist. Source: pkg/catalog/types.go (server network fields observed during inspection).
INVARIANT: A tool server's network capability is declared at registration and enforced at launch.
FAILURE_MODEL: Legitimate tools needing broad egress must be declared, which is operationally heavier; misdeclared hosts break tools.
SECURITY_MODEL: Blast-radius reduction: even a fully compromised tool server cannot reach undeclared hosts.
SCALING_MODEL: Enforced at container launch; zero per-call cost.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION sandbox for CRX tool servers; matches CRX's bounded-automation doctrine.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool server specs gain network-capability declarations enforced at launch.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: network policy enforcement in the tool-server launch path.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Containment for untrusted tool code; the strongest isolation mechanism found in the ecosystem.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Register a server with disableNetwork and a tool that fetches a URL; assert the fetch fails.

PROBLEM: OAuth browser flows for tool servers need human consent without handing the agent a raw browser or raw tokens.
MECHANISM: The OAuth interceptor opens the authorization URL and waits for the callback, gated on elicitation: the human confirms in a bounded, typed flow before tokens are issued to the gateway. Source: pkg/oauth/ (elicitation-gated browser flow observed during inspection).
INVARIANT: No token is issued without a human-confirmed, bounded elicitation round.
FAILURE_MODEL: Headless environments cannot complete the browser step; the flow has no non-interactive fallback by design.
SECURITY_MODEL: The agent never sees token material; the human authorizes at the identity provider, and the gateway receives tokens directly.
SCALING_MODEL: Human-latency per new authorization; tokens cached thereafter.
CRX_ANALOG: AUTHORIZATION link, human-in-the-loop credential grant for CRX missions; pairs with M07's elicitation pattern.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX gains a typed credential-grant state: the mission waits, the human authorizes, the runtime receives tokens without the agent touching them.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: elicitation UI plus OAuth callback plumbing in the mission runtime.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Human-consented tool credentials without exposing tokens to the agent or logs.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Decline the elicitation; assert no token is stored and the tool call fails with an authorization error, not a timeout.

PROBLEM: Per-tool authorization must be enforced at both discovery and execution, without leaking which tools exist but are forbidden.
MECHANISM: AuthorizationMiddleware (default deny) filters unauthorized tools from discovery listings and re-resolves and re-checks authorization immediately before execution, using the resolved access context; if no auth context exists it fails closed (deny). Listings return ambiguous not found or not authorized, preventing enumeration of forbidden tools. STDIO deliberately skips OAuth authorization as a trusted local-process boundary. Source: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/middleware/authorization.py (AuthCheck base, authorize() flow, discovery filtering, execution re-check, fail-closed default).
INVARIANT: Authorization is checked at discovery AND at execution; missing context denies; forbidden tools are indistinguishable from absent ones.
FAILURE_MODEL: Authorization is time-of-check: a revocation between the execution re-check and handler start is not covered; the re-check narrows but does not close the race.
SECURITY_MODEL: Default-deny, fail-closed, enumeration-resistant. The tool layer enforces decisions made by the auth context; it does not mint authority (contrast M35).
SCALING_MODEL: Two auth checks per call (discovery-filtered, then re-checked); context resolution cached per request.
CRX_ANALOG: AUTHORIZATION link, the strongest per-tool model found anywhere in the ecosystem. CRX ToolAuthority should mirror: filter at resolution, re-check at execution, fail closed on missing context, ambiguous denial.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool calls gain a two-gate authorization: resolution-time filtering plus execution-time re-check against fresh context.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: auth-context plumbing through the CRX tool boundary plus the double-check discipline.
EXPECTED_VALUE: The reference implementation for CRX's missing per-tool authorization; deny-by-default with enumeration resistance.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: List tools as an unauthorized identity and assert forbidden tools are absent (not flagged). Then call one directly and assert ambiguous not found or not authorized. Then drop the auth context entirely and assert deny.

PROBLEM: A tool name alone is ambiguous when multiple versions exist; callers need deterministic version resolution.
MECHANISM: Tools support version metadata and callers can request a specific version via VersionSpec; the server resolves the named tool to the requested version deterministically. Source: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/server.py (tool versioning and VersionSpec resolution observed during inspection).
INVARIANT: A (name, VersionSpec) pair resolves to exactly one tool implementation.
FAILURE_MODEL: An unsatisfiable VersionSpec fails at resolution, never silently falling back to another version.
SECURITY_MODEL: Version pinning supports the immutable (name, version) invariant (M11); callers cannot be silently upgraded.
SCALING_MODEL: Resolution cost per call; cacheable.
CRX_ANALOG: TOOL RESOLUTION. CRX tool refs should carry version specs resolved deterministically.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX ToolGateway resolution accepts version constraints and resolves them to exact immutable versions.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: version-spec parsing plus deterministic resolution.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Deterministic tool versioning for reproducible missions.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Request a tool with an unsatisfiable VersionSpec; assert resolution failure, not silent fallback.

PROBLEM: Unbounded tool responses can exhaust memory, blow up model context, and amplify result-poisoning attacks.
MECHANISM: ResponseLimitingMiddleware caps response size (max_bytes default 1 MB) and truncates or rejects oversized results. Source: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/middleware/response_limiting.py.
INVARIANT: No tool result larger than the configured bound reaches the agent.
FAILURE_MODEL: Truncation can cut mid-structure; callers must handle truncated receipts. The bound is a heuristic, not a semantic guarantee.
SECURITY_MODEL: Bounds resource exhaustion and context-poisoning blast radius from malicious servers.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-response size check; O(1).
CRX_ANALOG: RECEIPT link. CRX worker results reified as canonical events need size bounds before canonicalization.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX receipt records gain max-size bounds; oversized results become typed truncation events, not silent drops.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a size bound plus truncation handling on receipts.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Memory and context protection at the receipt boundary.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Return a 5 MB tool result; assert it is truncated or rejected at the bound.

PROBLEM: Server-side fetching of URLs (icons, schemas, remote resources) is an SSRF vector: DNS rebinding can redirect a safe-looking URL to internal infrastructure.
MECHANISM: ssrf.py implements SSRF-safe fetching with DNS pinning: the hostname is resolved once and the connection is pinned to the resolved IP, blocking DNS-rebinding attacks. Source: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/auth/ssrf.py.
INVARIANT: The IP the request goes to is the IP that was validated.
FAILURE_MODEL: CDN-backed hosts with rotating IPs can break pinning; the trade-off favors safety over availability.
SECURITY_MODEL: Closes the DNS-rebinding hole that naive allowlist fetching leaves open.
SCALING_MODEL: One DNS resolution per fetch; no connection-pool sharing across pins.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link: any CRX component that fetches remote resources on behalf of tools needs DNS-pinned fetching.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX outbound fetch gains DNS pinning as a mandatory property, not an option.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a pinned-fetch helper used by all outbound calls.
EXPECTED_VALUE: A concrete, reviewed SSRF defense instead of a hand-rolled one.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Point the fetcher at a hostname whose DNS flips between a public and a loopback IP mid-request; assert the request goes to the originally resolved IP.

PROBLEM: Unbounded tool-call rates let a runaway agent or a malicious client exhaust server resources.
MECHANISM: RateLimitingMiddleware applies a token-bucket limiter per client, bounding calls per time window. Source: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/middleware/rate_limiting.py.
INVARIANT: No client exceeds its configured rate; excess calls are rejected, not queued indefinitely.
FAILURE_MODEL: Aggressive limits can throttle legitimate bursts; limits are static, not adaptive.
SECURITY_MODEL: Bounds abuse from compromised or runaway agents; complements authentication.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-client bucket state; O(1) per call.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link: rate bounds on CRX tool invocation per mission/agent.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool calls gain per-agent rate budgets recorded on the mission.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a token-bucket limiter on the tool boundary.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Basic abuse resistance for autonomous tool use.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Exceed the configured rate; assert rejection with a rate-limit error, not silent queuing.

PROBLEM: Tool-call diagnostics must be structured and complete enough for audit without becoming a secret store.
MECHANISM: LoggingMiddleware records structured request lifecycle events (call start, arguments, result, duration, errors) in a machine-readable shape. Source: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/middleware/logging.py.
INVARIANT: Every tool call produces a structured lifecycle record.
FAILURE_MODEL: Structured logs still need the redact-before-log ordering (M19); structure alone does not prevent secret capture.
SECURITY_MODEL: Auditability for the EXECUTION link; pairs with secret scanning as a mandatory predecessor.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-call log record; volume-bounded by rate limiting (M30).
CRX_ANALOG: RECEIPT and EFFECT VERIFICATION links: CRX canonical tool-call events should be structured lifecycle records.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool-call events gain a structured lifecycle schema: start, args, receipt, duration, outcome.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a lifecycle event schema on the tool boundary.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Auditable tool execution: every call leaves a typed, queryable trace.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Execute a tool call and assert a structured record exists with start, arguments, result, duration, and outcome fields.

PROBLEM: A single client-side timeout conflates connection setup, handshake, and execution waits, making failures unactionable.
MECHANISM: The FastMCP client applies distinct timeouts per phase (connection, handshake/initialization, request round trip) rather than one global bound. Source: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/client/client.py (timeout parameters observed during inspection).
INVARIANT: A timeout names the phase that expired.
FAILURE_MODEL: Phase boundaries are approximate on multiplexed transports; the classification is best-effort, not exact.
SECURITY_MODEL: Phase-aware bounds limit slow-handshake resource holding distinctly from slow execution.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-phase timers; negligible overhead.
CRX_ANALOG: EXECUTION link. CRX TIMED_OUT events (M06) should name the phase: connect, authorize, execute, receipt.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX timeout events gain a phase field.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: phase labels on timeout budgets and events.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Actionable timeout diagnostics instead of one opaque deadline.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Stall the handshake while keeping the connection alive; assert the timeout names the handshake phase.

PROBLEM: Tool definitions are the primary prompt-injection and tool-poisoning vector; they must be inspected before any call.
MECHANISM: agent-scan statically inspects tool definitions (names, descriptions, schemas) through analysis pipelines before the agent ever invokes them, flagging injection and poisoning patterns. Source: src/agent_scan/inspect.py, src/agent_scan/pipelines.py, src/agent_scan/direct_scanner.py.
INVARIANT: No tool is invoked before its definition has been scanned.
FAILURE_MODEL: Static analysis misses novel obfuscation; scanning is a heuristic gate, not a proof of safety.
SECURITY_MODEL: Treats tool definitions as untrusted input (consistent with M02); shifts some trust from runtime to inspection time.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-tool scan at discovery; cacheable per (server, tool, version).
CRX_ANALOG: ACTION INTENT link. CRX tool intake should scan definitions before cataloguing.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool catalog entries gain a scan verdict; unscanned tools are not resolvable.
INTEGRATION_COST: M: a scan pipeline plus verdict storage on catalog entries.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Pre-execution screening for the highest-risk input in the MCP threat model.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Register a tool whose description contains an indirect prompt injection; assert the scan flags it before any invocation.

PROBLEM: Human approval prompts for tool calls often display raw arguments, leaking secrets and environment data to the approver's screen and logs.
MECHANISM: agent-scan redacts environment values, header values, and query values in consent/approval displays, so the human sees the action shape but not the secret material. Source: src/agent_scan/redact.py, src/agent_scan/consent.py.
INVARIANT: Secret-typed values are never rendered in approval surfaces.
FAILURE_MODEL: Redaction is pattern-based; novel secret formats may display in the clear.
SECURITY_MODEL: Approval UIs are a disclosure surface; redaction shrinks what a shoulder-surfer or log-scraper can capture.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-display redaction; O(payload).
CRX_ANALOG: AUTHORIZATION link: CRX human-approval surfaces for tool calls must redact secret-typed values.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX approval prompts render redacted argument shapes; the full values stay in the secure channel.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a redaction pass on approval rendering.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Approval without exposure: humans authorize actions, not secrets.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Trigger an approval prompt for a call containing an API key argument; assert the displayed prompt shows the key redacted.

PROBLEM: A tempting shortcut is to let tool metadata (annotations, descriptions) decide whether a call is authorized: the tool layer becomes the authority.
MECHANISM: This design is REJECTED by the harvest rule and by the spec text in source: ToolAnnotations are explicitly untrusted hints and clients should never make tool-use decisions based on them (src/mcp-types/mcp_types/_v2026_07_28/__init__.py:1076). Any CRX design in which annotation parsing, description scanning, or tool self-attestation grants execution authority violates ACTION INTENT -> AUTHORIZATION separation and must be classified HARVEST_CLASS=REJECT.
INVARIANT: The tool layer never decides authorization; it enforces decisions made by an external authority.
FAILURE_MODEL: Not applicable: this row records an anti-pattern, not a mechanism.
SECURITY_MODEL: Annotation-trusting authorization is a confused-deputy vulnerability by construction: the party being authorized (the tool) supplies the evidence of its own authorization.
SCALING_MODEL: Not applicable.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX ToolAuthority must remain an external decider; ToolGateway enforces. Any proposal to auto-authorize based on readOnlyHint or description content is REJECT.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX authorization decisions may consume annotations as signals but never as authority; the decision record names the actual authority.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: a lint/architecture rule plus review of any annotation-consuming code path.
EXPECTED_VALUE: A named, citable rejection that prevents the most likely authorization shortcut in CRX tool work.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Propose a design where readOnlyHint=true auto-approves execution; assert it is classified REJECT under the harvest rule.

PROBLEM: Transient failures tempt generic blind retry of tool calls; without idempotency or side-effect classification, retries duplicate real-world effects.
MECHANISM: pkg/retry/retry.go implements a generic retry helper that retries every error without idempotency keys, without side-effect classification, and without distinguishing transport failure from application failure. Used around tool execution paths, this would retry non-idempotent calls and duplicate effects. Recorded as an anti-pattern: retry belongs at the transport layer (M05, bounded, resume-based) and must never be applied generically at the tool-call layer.
INVARIANT: Tool-call retries require idempotency evidence; generic retry is never safe at the execution layer.
FAILURE_MODEL: Not applicable: this row records an anti-pattern, not a mechanism.
SECURITY_MODEL: Blind retry converts a transient failure into a duplicated side effect, which is an integrity violation at the EFFECT VERIFICATION link.
SCALING_MODEL: Not applicable.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX must not wrap tool execution in generic retry; retries require idempotency keys (absent across the whole ecosystem, per the proven gap) or explicit non-idempotent classification with no-retry semantics.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX tool-call records gain an idempotency classification; the runtime refuses to retry calls lacking idempotency evidence.
INTEGRATION_COST: S: an idempotency-classification field plus a no-generic-retry rule on the execution path.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Prevents duplicated real-world effects, the most expensive failure class in autonomous tool use.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Wrap a non-idempotent tool call in the generic retry helper, inject one transient failure, and assert the side effect executes twice, documenting the hazard.
